This page is the **working tracker**: what's in flight, in what order, with technical detail. For the plain-language case — what the program delivers and why it's worth the time — see [The Program](program.qmd). Rationale for individual choices lives in the [decision log](decisions.qmd).

## Where we stand (September 2026)

The ecosystem is a barbell. One end: a scientifically sophisticated core (`jheem2`, ~75k lines) with no automated test gate, no CI, and several very large files. The other end contains a mature artifact-promotion subsystem: digest-promoted containers with golden and perturbation tests, feeding release-versioned data and the portal. The missing middle is the work. One complete exemplar — the container platform — and one partial upstream exemplar — the syphilis manager's gated assembly-and-promotion path — show modern practice already succeeds in this ecosystem.

The sequencing is also informed by earlier exploratory refactoring analysis
(archived [here](archive/index.qmd)). Reconstructing an earlier calibration
remains an explicit publication need, with SHIELD as the first reference workflow
([D-019](decisions.qmd)). Two narrower deliverables now have direct team interest:
a SHIELD container pilot and CI for assembling the HIV surveillance manager
([D-020](decisions.qmd#d-020)).
Neither is equivalent to a claim of end-to-end reproducibility or raw-data-to-final
automation. The sampler seed/resume finding remains relevant to a later
deterministic-replay claim, but is not a prerequisite for establishing a bounded
container runtime. Calibration observability and functional-form documentation
remain open. The broader program is still a working engineering proposal rather
than a team-adopted plan ([D-017](decisions.qmd)).

### Practice baseline (updated 2026-09-22)

Per-repo engineering practice, as verifiable facts. This table is the program's "before" picture and its progress tracker — cells flip as work lands ([D-014](decisions.qmd)).

| Repo | README | Tests | CI | Release discipline |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jheem2` | — | 100 recursive test/reprex/profiling artifacts; 0 automated gate | — | manual version bumps on master, no git tags ([D-012](decisions.qmd)) |
| `jheem_analyses` | no root README | syphilis structural validation plus SHIELD static/unit/model tests | 3 syphilis-manager workflows plus SHIELD model-test workflow; recent SHIELD runs stop at the failing static tier | n/a (scripts) |
| `bayesian.simulations` | — | — | — | — |
| `distributions` | — | — | — | — |
| `locations` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | — |
| `jheem-containers` | ✅ | smoke + golden + perturbation | build → test-by-digest → promote | fail-closed digest promotion, semver |
| `jheem-base` | ✅ | via container cascade | ✅ | semver tags |
| `jheem-backend` | ✅ | — | 8 workflows | — |
| `jheem-portal` | ✅ | — | hosted deploys | — |
| `jheem-simulations` | ✅ | n/a | n/a | semver GitHub Releases with documented deprecations |

The modeling core still has much less automated protection than the delivery
platform, but it is no longer accurate to say that only syphilis-manager CI exists
there. The new SHIELD suite contains deliberately failing findings; a red run does
not currently distinguish a new regression from those open findings, and later
tiers are skipped when the static tier fails. See the
[workflow](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/16eff985372fd65be46871bf164acb6eff14beb3/.github/workflows/test-shield.yml),
[suite status](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/16eff985372fd65be46871bf164acb6eff14beb3/applications/SHIELD/tests/README.md),
and [2026-09-22 run](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/actions/runs/35762822719).

### Next

The immediate work is two bounded tracks. For SHIELD, review the opt-in recorded
route, reconcile its entrypoint and fixture with the older container canary, then
demonstrate a pinned image on a team server with explicit inputs, storage mounts,
failure reporting, checkpoint continuation, and inspectable outputs. This does
not yet establish uninterrupted/resumed equality or production-scale assembly.
For HIV surveillance, the first manual hosted merge has established a candidate
and measured its Linux resource use. Next review the two structural warnings and
an active-consumer validation baseline, then publish a versioned candidate with
its inputs, logs, and validation report before any promotion. The released
sections, verified movement archive, and pinned census manager form a declared
section-to-final input set, but their upstream raw-to-section lineage remains
open. The seed/resume evidence and scientific likelihood questions remain open;
neither should be silently resolved by container or manager-pipeline changes.

- **Package-mode and CI feasibility** — use the toy fixture and the actual
  `jheem_analyses` loading path to measure what prevents `library(jheem2)`, what a
  minimal automated check would catch, and what it costs to maintain. General
  CI across every repository is not a standalone team priority; targeted SHIELD
  and HIV-manager checks now answer specific team needs. A verification net
  remains a prerequisite before behavior-changing engine or sampler work
  ([D-001](decisions.qmd), [D-017](decisions.qmd)).
- **Select the reference application** whose complete path — raw data → data manager → calibration → simset → container extraction → portal/manuscript artifact — becomes the paved road other applications later migrate through ([D-015](decisions.qmd)). Leading candidate: Ryan White (active, published, portal-facing, already the worked example in [Application Anatomy](application-anatomy.qmd)).
- **NAMESPACE export sweep** — team specs call non-exported jheem2 functions unqualified. At `jheem_analyses@426f03d1`, the EHE spec calls `create.logistic.taper.functional.form`; at `jheem2@90b68ad`, that function is defined but not exported. This blocks `library(jheem2)` for spec sourcing. The sweep unblocks package mode as the default workflow and shrinks the per-session C++ recompile / toolchain-sensitivity surface. (The originally cited example, `create.solver.metadata`, had become exported by `jheem2@90b68ad` — caught by an external re-audit; a reminder that unpinned claims rot, per [D-014](decisions.qmd).)
- **Fix the `populate_outcomes_array` C++ undefined behavior** — no longer merely latent: at `jheem-containers@9c846bf`, the container runtime hot-patches this function in production via `assignInNamespace` (`base/common/custom_simulation.R:122`), so the platform already carries a live workaround for a bug filed as deferred. Fix on `dev` once the package/CI verification net exists, gate with the container golden suite, then retire the patch. A sanitizer pass (ASan/UBSan) over the C++ follows once CI exists.
- **Automatic run history and provenance receipts** — reconcile the staged SHIELD receipt with current application and sampler work, then inspect it on the bounded server pilot. A readable summary plus validated JSON should record engine/analyses commits, support-package versions, data-manager identities, image or environment identity, run configuration, seeds, and output digests. Capture remains local-first; archival is automatic and retryable, and promoted artifacts must resolve back to their receipt ([D-015](decisions.qmd)).
- **Gate the unguarded `browser()` calls** at `JHEEM_engine.R` ~4597/~4647 — they fire during *normal* intervention runs under `Rscript` (harmless but noisy; outputs verified bit-identical). The correct `if (debug)` pattern already exists at line ~1739.
- **Quickstart vignette** on the toy fixture (spec → engine → simulate → plot), executed in CI.
- **`@examples` on the top ~50 exports**, chosen by usage-grep of `jheem_analyses`/`jheem2_interactive` — doubles as API curation (public vs. `@keywords internal`).
- **pkgdown site** for jheem2, linked from this wiki.
- **Focused regression coverage for the calibration hook** — prove unchanged
  sampling when no policy is configured, resumable checkpoint-boundary stopping,
  and deterministic policy decisions before enabling early termination on routine
  runs.
- **Complete syphilis raw-to-final automation and extend manager CI upstream** — the syphilis raw-data→section stage still runs outside the hosted merge workflow. The first HIV surveillance slice should similarly label its prebuilt-section boundary rather than claiming a full raw-to-final pipeline. Broader census and surveillance-manager graduation remains open ([D-004](decisions.qmd), refined by [D-015](decisions.qmd)).
- **Custom domain for this site** (`docs.jheem.org`) once the team is using it.

### Later / deferred

- **Structural decomposition of jheem2** ([D-003](decisions.qmd)) — revisit after API curation and tests; extraction becomes cheap and optional rather than heroic.
- **Platform org-ownership migration** and a **second operator** able to run at least one delivery workflow end-to-end (bus-factor mitigation; coupled to [D-010](decisions.qmd)).
- Retire source-mode loading of jheem2 in favor of `library()` + `devtools::load_all()`.
- Format-versioned data-manager representation (reduce serialized-R6 fragility).
- Release hygiene for jheem2: git tags on master version bumps, a NEWS.md, and (once CI exists) a version-monotonicity check ([D-012](decisions.qmd)).
- Hygiene sweep: `browser()` calls behind a debug flag, condition-object error capture replacing `.GlobalEnv` writes, `R/tests` and `R/beta_code` moved out of `R/`.

## Success criteria

- Any jheem2 PR gets an automated verdict (check + regression) before merge.
- A new contributor runs the quickstart end-to-end in under 30 minutes with nothing but the package.
- A running calibration can be inspected (likelihood behavior, mixing, per-city status) without asking anyone.
- The ecosystem map exists, is current, and is linked from every repo's README.
- A three-month interruption costs re-reading this wiki, not re-deriving it.

## Standing risks

- **Planning outpacing shipping:** documentation and planning feel like progress without changing anything. Mitigation: wiki work is time-boxed and tied to a named next implementation increment and acceptance check; the public status changes only as evidence lands.
- **Fixture turns out hard:** fallback recorded in [D-008](decisions.qmd).
- **Continuity:** the effort must tolerate interruptions — small merges, state recorded in this wiki, and a current map from which anyone can re-orient.
- **Two-speed masking:** platform polish must not substitute for core legibility; both ends of the barbell move.
